sources.title: 01 Bharat KALP Framework - Focused Revision V5
02 Bharat KALP - Learning Objectives and Assessment Alignment
03 Bharat KALP - Assessment Activities and Evidence Alignment
05 Bharat KALP - Response Examples and Rater Calibration
06 Bharat KALP - Learning Principles and Implementation Checks

instructions: Use the supplied facts for these fictional cases. Notes, online resources and generative AI are allowed without penalty. Research is optional and must not replace the case facts. Reviewers interpret your response with this assistance allowed.

Use bullets or short paragraphs to explain your reasoning. There is no timer or word limit. Writing polish, length, framework names and number of sources are not scored. Different choices can be defensible. Label any assumptions you make.

You can pause and resume in this browser. Submit your initial response to reveal the update. Each submitted version becomes read-only and remains available. An update may keep a sound decision or explanation; changing your answer is not required.
Human feedback becomes available after all four cases are submitted or you explicitly end early, and only after a reviewer reviews your evidence. There is no overall score or pass/fail result.

objectives.title: Strategic choice
objectives.text: Select and justify a governance response by weighing alternatives, constraints, and near- and longer-term consequences.
objectives.evidence: Explains why the selected response serves the stated public goal better than a credible alternative, using relevant case evidence and consequences across time horizons.
objectives.mapping: A-R1: Comparative strategic choice. Primary A.P1; supplementary comparative evidence A.P5. No preferred policy answer.
objectives.boundary: A chosen action without comparative reasons does not establish this objective. Grammar and confidence are not scored.

objectives.title: Ethical and citizen-centred justification
objectives.text: Justify a governance choice when public duties and citizen interests conflict, accounting for who benefits, who bears harm, and relevant safeguards.
objectives.metrics: Ethical Reasoning; Public Service Orientation (Seva Bhav)
objectives.evidence: Identifies the material ethical tension, explains effects on affected citizen groups, and gives a public-interest rationale with proportionate safeguards.
objectives.mapping: A-R2: Ethical deliberation; A-R3: Citizen impacts and safeguards. Primary A.P2; supplementary A.P6. Different defensible choices can meet the criteria.
objectives.boundary: Naming a value, claiming good intentions or agreeing with the assessor is insufficient. This does not establish intrinsic motivation or stable personal integrity.

objectives.title: Implementation feasibility
objectives.text: Develop a feasible implementation approach that accounts for institutional responsibilities, coordination needs, and likely barriers.
objectives.evidence: Assigns actions to actors with relevant authority, explains dependencies and foreseeable resistance, and proposes a workable response to a material barrier.
objectives.mapping: A-R4: Institutional feasibility. Primary A.P3; supplementary A.P6. Judge implementation reasoning, not procedural detail.
objectives.boundary: A plan is evidence of planning, not actual stakeholder influence, team leadership or workplace delivery. Provide necessary mandate information when specialist knowledge is not the target.

objectives.title: Adaptive judgement
objectives.text: Distinguish a problem addressable through established procedures from a challenge requiring learning or experimentation, and adjust the response as new evidence emerges.
objectives.evidence: Justifies what can be addressed procedurally and what remains uncertain or requires stakeholder learning, then explains which parts of the response should be retained, revised or investigated.
objectives.mapping: A-R5: Challenge diagnosis (primary A.P4; supplementary A.P5); A-R6: Adaptation from new information (A.P5-A.P6 compared with initial response). Justified retention can be strong.
objectives.boundary: Changing an answer alone is not adaptive leadership. A technical or mixed response may be appropriate; do not reward ambiguity or experimentation regardless of need.

objectives.title: Causal explanation
objectives.text: Explain a governance problem using a plausible causal account that distinguishes symptoms from drivers and includes relevant interdependencies.
objectives.evidence: Links observed conditions to plausible mechanisms and explains how relevant actors, incentives or feedback affect the problem.
objectives.mapping: B-R1: Causal account and systems coherence. Primary B.P1. Judge relevance and plausibility, not counts of causes or arrows.
objectives.boundary: Listing stakeholders or asserting a root cause without a causal account is insufficient. A plausible account remains a hypothesis until tested.

objectives.title: Testable prediction
objectives.text: Predict how a proposed intervention will affect a governance system, stating the mechanism, assumptions, and observable evidence that would test the prediction.
objectives.evidence: States an expected change, explains the causal pathway, identifies a material assumption and specifies a meaningful observation that could support or challenge the prediction.
objectives.mapping: B-R2: Testable causal prediction. Primary B.P2. Prediction accuracy alone is insufficient.
objectives.boundary: A lucky correct prediction or vague claim that things will improve is insufficient. Do not add specialist forecasting demands that the case does not support.

objectives.title: Evidence interpretation
objectives.text: Evaluate whether observed results support a proposed causal explanation, considering alternative explanations and limits in the data.
objectives.evidence: Compares the claim with relevant results, distinguishes observation from causal inference, and evaluates a credible alternative explanation or measurement limitation.
objectives.mapping: B-R3: Evidence-to-claim reasoning. Primary B.P3, compared with B.P2. Interpretation differs from original model plausibility.
objectives.boundary: A change in an indicator does not alone establish policy success or causation. When relevant, examine denominators, timeframes, selection effects or incentives.

objectives.title: Justified revision
objectives.text: Revise or retain a causal explanation and proposed intervention in light of new evidence, explaining the decision and remaining uncertainty.
objectives.evidence: Identifies which prior assumption the evidence bears on, makes a warranted revision or explains why retention is justified, and states what further evidence is needed.
objectives.mapping: B-R4: Justified model and action update. Primary B.P4, compared with B.P1-B.P2 and the supplied intervention. Judge warranted revision/retention, not size of change.
objectives.boundary: A revised answer demonstrates reasoning within this task, not a stable learning-agility trait or programme-level leadership growth. If B-LO3 is weak, still examine the updating evidence directly rather than automatically duplicating that penalty.

criteria.title: Comparative strategic choice
criteria.alignment: Alignment: A-LO1; Strategic Thinking; Decision Quality & Justification. Evidence: A.P1; relevant comparative evidence in A.P5.

descriptors.Developing: Justifies a choice using a single demand or assertion of priority; the offered comparison overlooks a material constraint or consequence, so preference is not supported by the case.
descriptors.Emerging: Uses relevant goals and constraints to compare a credible alternative, but a material trade-off or consequence across the case's time horizons remains insufficiently explained.
descriptors.Proficient: Explains why the choice better serves the public goal than a credible alternative, weighing material constraints and immediate and longer consequences. Identifies the consequential trade-off or uncertainty affecting that preference.

criteria.boundary: Judge the comparison and strategic rationale, not a preferred allocation or a numerical optimisation. An answer may be concise and use conditional decisions.

criteria.title: Ethical deliberation
criteria.alignment: Alignment: A-LO2; Ethical Reasoning. Evidence: A.P2; relevant changes in A.P6.

descriptors.Developing: Treats a material conflict of duties as if only one duty matters, or invokes a value without explaining why it warrants the choice in the case.
descriptors.Emerging: Recognises competing duties and gives a relevant reason for the choice, but does not adequately explain how the competing duty constrains the response or what ethical cost is accepted.
descriptors.Proficient: Explains the material competing duties and a defensible public-interest basis for the choice, including how the competing duty is accommodated or why the residual ethical cost is justified.

criteria.boundary: Judge reasoning about duties, not virtue, declared intentions, named ethical frameworks or agreement with the assessor. Concrete harm and safeguards are judged under A-R3.

criteria.title: Citizen impacts and safeguards
criteria.alignment: Alignment: A-LO2; Public Service Orientation (Seva Bhav). Evidence: A.P2; relevant changes in A.P6.

descriptors.Developing: Assumes an apparently uniform response affects citizens equally or dismisses a material affected group; proposed safeguards do not address the harm created by the choice.
descriptors.Emerging: Explains a relevant differential citizen impact and proposes a related safeguard, but a material access barrier, burden or practical safeguard limitation remains unresolved in the reasoning.
descriptors.Proficient: Explains who benefits and who bears a material burden, including relevant access differences, and justifies feasible, proportionate safeguards that address those effects while recognising remaining limits.

criteria.boundary: Judge attention to citizen effects demonstrated in the response. Do not require every conceivable group or infer intrinsic motivation. Safeguards can differ across defensible policies.

criteria.title: Institutional feasibility
criteria.alignment: Alignment: A-LO3; Institutional Awareness. Evidence: A.P3; relevant changes in A.P6.

descriptors.Developing: Proposes delivery through actors without the supplied authority or relies on resources or coordination that contradict a material case constraint, making the proposed approach unworkable.
descriptors.Emerging: Assigns relevant responsibilities and identifies a real dependency or barrier, but a material coordination step, authority issue or response to the barrier is too incomplete to establish feasibility.
descriptors.Proficient: Assigns actions consistently with the supplied responsibilities, explains material dependencies, and provides a feasible way to handle a likely barrier through coordination, sequencing or appropriate escalation.

criteria.boundary: Do not reward procedural detail for its own sake. Judge the plan, not actual implementation, influence or stakeholder engagement.

criteria.title: Challenge diagnosis
criteria.alignment: Alignment: A-LO4; Adaptive Leadership, sampled diagnostic aspect. Evidence: A.P4; changes to diagnosis in A.P5.

descriptors.Developing: Treats a material trust, expectation or participation challenge as solvable solely by an instruction or technical fix, or proposes learning when an established procedural response would address the identified issue without explaining why.
descriptors.Emerging: Distinguishes an operational issue from a challenge requiring people to learn or change, but the explanation of why they differ or how the response matches that diagnosis is incomplete.
descriptors.Proficient: Explains what existing expertise or procedures can address and what requires learning or changed behaviour, and connects each to an appropriate response. Recognises mixed challenges where the case warrants them.

criteria.boundary: Technical and adaptive labels are not required. Naming a category without reasoning is insufficient; experimentation is not inherently superior to established practice.

criteria.title: Adaptation from new information
criteria.alignment: Alignment: A-LO4; Adaptive Leadership, sampled response aspect. Evidence: A.P5; implications and reconsideration evidence in A.P6.

descriptors.Developing: Changes or retains the response for reasons that ignore or contradict the material update; reconsideration conditions do not bear on the decision.
descriptors.Emerging: Links a change or retention to relevant new information, but leaves an important implication for the plan unexplained or gives a reconsideration condition too vague to guide action.
descriptors.Proficient: Explains proportionate revision, retention or investigation in light of the material update and prior reasoning; carries the relevant implications into the response and identifies evidence that would warrant reconsideration.

criteria.boundary: Rate the update process directly. Do not reward size of change or automatically repeat an initial-decision weakness. Challenge diagnosis is judged separately under A-R5.

criteria.title: Causal account and systems coherence
criteria.alignment: Alignment: B-LO1; Quality of Analysis; Systems Thinking. Evidence: B.P1.

descriptors.Developing: Explains the problem through an unsupported association or asserted cause; the account cannot explain a material relationship between actors, incentives or observed conditions in the case.
descriptors.Emerging: Provides a plausible mechanism connecting relevant conditions to the problem, but an important interdependency or distinction between symptom and driver is underdeveloped.
descriptors.Proficient: Distinguishes the observed problem from plausible drivers and explains a coherent mechanism, including material interdependencies or feedback where relevant to the case. Treats untested causal claims as hypotheses.

criteria.boundary: Judge relevance and coherence, not the number of causes, arrows or stakeholders. A short narrative is sufficient. Do not require a feedback loop if it is immaterial to the explanation.

criteria.title: Testable causal prediction
criteria.alignment: Alignment: B-LO2; Systems Thinking, sampled predictive aspect. Evidence: B.P2.

descriptors.Developing: Predicts improvement or deterioration without a mechanism connecting the intervention to that effect, or proposes an observation that cannot meaningfully support or challenge the prediction or test a material assumption.
descriptors.Emerging: Links an expected effect to a plausible mechanism and gives a relevant assumption or observation, but the connection between the assumption, prediction and potential test is incomplete.
descriptors.Proficient: Connects an expected effect to a plausible mechanism, states a material assumption and identifies an observation that could support or challenge the prediction. Addresses a material indirect effect when warranted by the account.

criteria.boundary: Do not require exact numerical forecasts or reward a lucky correct outcome. The test must be informative for the stated claim, not necessarily a complete evaluation design.

criteria.title: Evidence-to-claim reasoning
criteria.alignment: Alignment: B-LO3; Critical Analysis. Evidence: B.P3, compared with the B.P2 prediction.

descriptors.Developing: Treats the reported result as proving the intervention's causal success or failure despite a material alternative explanation or mismatch between the indicator and public goal.
descriptors.Emerging: Compares results with the prediction and identifies a credible limitation or alternative, but does not sufficiently explain how it changes the conclusion that the evidence warrants.
descriptors.Proficient: Explains how results bear on the prediction, weighs a material alternative explanation or measurement limit, and states a conclusion proportionate to what the observations can and cannot establish.

criteria.boundary: Do not reward generic scepticism. A specific supported conclusion can be strong; a before/after difference alone is not attribution. Statistical significance calculations are not required.

criteria.title: Justified model and action update
criteria.alignment: Alignment: B-LO4; Learning Agility, sampled task-level aspect. Evidence: B.P4, compared with B.P1/B.P2 and the case's supplied intervention.

descriptors.Developing: Replaces or retains the explanation or action without a warranted connection to the new evidence; the proposed next step repeats the same untested assumption rather than addressing the relevant uncertainty.
descriptors.Emerging: Identifies a relevant assumption to revise or retain and proposes a plausible next action, but the evidence-to-update connection or the next informative test remains incomplete.
descriptors.Proficient: Identifies the assumption or causal pathway affected by the evidence, justifies revision or retention of the model and action, and proposes a next test or observation directed at a consequential remaining uncertainty.

criteria.boundary: Retention can be Proficient. Judge the updating demonstrated, not personality, programme growth, admission of error or the amount rewritten. The action target is the supplied intervention; do not require an earlier officer-authored plan that B.P1/B.P2 did not elicit. Do not automatically carry the B-R3 rating into this criterion.

rubricRules: Record a descriptive judgement for each criterion in each case, with a response excerpt or precise location and a short rationale. Read the relevant evidence across the indicated prompts; do not treat each prompt as an additional score. A1 and A2 each produce six criterion observations; B1 and B2 each produce four. Twenty observations are possible when all four cases yield usable evidence, but completion does not guarantee evidence for every criterion.

Developing describes an observable weakness in the targeted reasoning. Emerging describes relevant reasoning with a material unresolved link. Proficient describes a supported reasoning relationship under the case conditions. The actual criterion descriptors below govern the judgement. Do not rate by prose length, counts of facts mentioned or minor omissions that do not affect the reasoning.

For mixed evidence, identify which central reasoning relationship is supported and which remains unresolved. Select the descriptor that best explains the material evidence and record the boundary issue. If a defensible choice between levels is unavailable, mark review status Uncertain, record the competing interpretations and seek review. Uncertain is neither a proficiency level nor a low-performance judgement; do not invent a midpoint or use an automatic lowest-level rule.

Use Insufficient evidence when the submitted evidence, including relevant reasoning elsewhere in the same phase, does not reveal the criterion. Use Not elicited when a task, reveal or technical failure prevented the opportunity. These are evidence statuses, not fourth proficiency levels. An attempted response demonstrating a specific misconception can be Developing; a blank field alone cannot. If a prior response needed for comparison is unavailable, record the affected limitation and appropriate status rather than inventing prior reasoning.

Phase attribution: A-R1-A-R5 use the stated initial prompt as primary evidence; relevant A.P5/A.P6 evidence is supplementary. B-R1 and B-R2 use B.P1 and B.P2. A-R6 uses A.P5/A.P6 compared with the initial response; B-R3 uses B.P3 compared with B.P2; B-R4 uses B.P4 compared with B.P1/B.P2 and the supplied intervention. Keep the initial judgement visible when later evidence adds, repairs or contradicts reasoning, and identify the later prompt and phase in the same criterion profile. Do not average phases, silently replace the initial judgement or create extra prompt scores. If material conflict prevents a defensible overall description, use Uncertain review status. The primary prompt mapping identifies the intended elicitation location, not an exclusive evidence box. Relevant reasoning elsewhere in the same phase can contribute if the actual prompt/location is recorded. Keep attribution to the phase in which it appeared; do not infer an initial capability from an update or count repeated wording as independent evidence.
feedbackRule: Use a compact record: case and criterion; task/rubric version and prompt/phase; observed evidence; descriptor-based judgement or evidence status and any Uncertain review status; a specific strength or unresolved reasoning link; and a relevant next opportunity where available. Preserve material differences between initial and later evidence. Do not describe the officer's character. Deliver feedback after diagnostic completion or explicit end, following documents 03 and 06. When evidence is insufficient or was not elicited, explain the limitation and offer another opportunity to elicit the reasoning; do not invent a deficit. When judgement is Uncertain, arrange review of the competing interpretations. Targeted practice is optional and pending; do not promise an unavailable task or generate placeholder coaching.

phases.title: Initial response
facts: Role and goal: you coordinate the metropolitan emergency transport response. Protect life and essential access over the next six hours and recommend a credible continuity direction for the next 72 hours. You can coordinate bus redeployment; districts run evacuation and shelters, the transport authority controls services, police secure routes, and health authorities organise hospital fuel. Transport asset reopening requires the relevant agency's safety clearance. Your role does not authorise overriding that clearance.

Initial facts: flooding has disrupted normal routes for about 140,000 commuters. About 11,000 residents are under evacuation advisory. There are 600 buses available for emergency redeployment. Districts request 420 for evacuation and shelter movement; the rail authority requests 260 for stranded passengers. These requests exceed available capacity.

Two major public hospitals have about eight hours of backup-generator fuel. Police can secure only two priority corridors at a time. Mobile connectivity is degraded in 40% of the affected area. Flooded metro assets await inspection. The weather service estimates a 60% chance of additional heavy rain over the next 12 hours.

Some residents are reluctant to evacuate because they distrust conflicting official messages and fear losing possessions. Districts can arrange property-security patrols and shelter assistance, but must coordinate with police and local representatives. The case does not assume that issuing another evacuation instruction will resolve the reluctance.
phases.task: Answer all four questions. You may prioritise requests, sequence deployment or propose another feasible response. There is no requirement to split capacity equally or satisfy every request immediately.

prompts.label: Choose and compare
prompts.text: What response do you recommend? Explain why it serves the public goal better than a credible alternative. Consider the constraints and consequences over both the immediate and longer time horizons.

prompts.label: Citizen impacts and duties
prompts.text: Where does your choice create a tension between public duties and citizen interests? Explain who benefits, who may bear harm, and the safeguards you would use.

prompts.label: Put the response into practice
prompts.text: How would you carry out the response? Identify the actors and their responsibilities, the coordination dependencies that matter, and a feasible way to address a likely barrier.

prompts.label: Understand the challenge
prompts.text: Which parts can established procedures or available expertise address? Which parts, if any, require people to learn or change how they act? Explain why and how your approach addresses each kind of challenge.

phases.title: Update response
facts: Update, revealed after initial submission: three hours later, the rail request falls from 260 to 180 buses because an unaffected terminal has added trains. One flooded metro tunnel will remain closed today. The largest shelter district will reach capacity within two hours unless additional space is opened. The chance of further heavy rain falls to 35%; it has not fallen to zero. Local representatives report that carers are avoiding shelters because arrangements for dependants are unclear.

phases.title: Initial response
facts: Role and goal: you coordinate a fictional national LPG continuity response. Maintain essential access over the next seven days and recommend a feasible 30-day strategy. Supply companies allocate available stock and manage dispatch; states coordinate local distribution and complaints. Emergency price or subsidy changes require finance and legal approval. The case provides the authority needed for reasoning; recall of actual LPG rules is not expected.

Initial facts: an import disruption may last two to five weeks. Usable national inventory equals about 18 days of normal consumption. Eight highly affected states have about seven days of stock, while less affected states have about 25 days. Redistribution is possible, but freight capacity limits how quickly stock can move.

Hospitals and community kitchens depend on LPG for essential services. Many low-income households have no safe alternative fuel and cannot readily pay more. A uniform refill restriction is administratively simple but would apply to both essential and discretionary use. Allocating stock mainly through higher prices could reduce demand but may exclude households unable to pay.

Reports of shortages have led some households to seek early refills. Supply companies can publish verified availability; local distributors and states would need to coordinate explanations and complaints handling. Current dispatch procedures alone do not address expectations or trust. Unsafe substitution must not be treated as an acceptable solution.
phases.task: Answer all four questions. You may prioritise essential uses, redistribute stock, manage demand or combine approaches. Explain a credible alternative to your choice rather than assuming one allocation policy is mandatory.

phases.title: Initial response
facts: Role and problem: you advise a city on reducing residents' exposure to fine-particle air pollution. PM2.5 is a measure of fine-particle concentration; lower values indicate less pollution at the monitor. Traffic contributes to pollution, but weather and other sources also affect measured concentrations. Exposure depends on where people live and spend time.

Initial facts: two central zones have high monitor readings and heavy diesel freight traffic. Nearby residential roads could receive diverted trucks. The proposed intervention restricts daytime diesel freight access in the two zones, with essential-service exemptions and enforcement by the transport authority. It does not reduce the total amount of freight that must move.

The city will observe central-zone monitor readings, comparison-zone readings and truck counts on nearby residential roads. The comparison zones will not receive the restriction, but differ in traffic and land use. Initial seven-day average PM2.5 values are 120 units in the intervention zones and 100 in the comparison zones. No claim is made that these zones are equivalent.
phases.task: Answer both questions. Predict consequences for the stated goal of reducing resident exposure, rather than treating an improvement at one monitor as the whole goal.

prompts.label: Explain the causes
prompts.text: Explain how the problem is produced. Distinguish observed symptoms from plausible drivers, and show relevant links between actors, incentives or feedback. A short narrative is enough; a diagram is optional and receives no extra credit.

prompts.label: Predict and test
prompts.text: What effects do you expect if the proposed intervention is implemented as described, and through what mechanism? State a material assumption and an observation that would support or challenge your prediction. Explain a relevant indirect effect where your account warrants one. Precise numerical forecasts are not required.

phases.title: Initial response
facts: Role and problem: you advise a department seeking to resolve citizens' service grievances. Closing a ticket is an administrative status; resolving the underlying problem is the public goal. Citizens may submit again if a grievance is closed without resolution.

Initial facts: the department has a backlog. A proposed reform introduces a dashboard ranking offices by the proportion of tickets closed within seven days. Supervisors will review that ranking each week. Staff can close a ticket after recording an action, even when the citizen has not confirmed that the issue is resolved. Citizen follow-up is feasible but currently separate from the dashboard.

Before reform, 2,000 tickets are registered in a month and 60% are closed within seven days. An independent random follow-up sample of 200 citizens finds that 56% report their underlying problem resolved. The dashboard measures speed and status, not verified resolution.
phases.task: Answer both questions. Explain how the proposed incentive might affect staff behaviour, citizens and recorded performance. Consider that faster handling could help as well as create unintended incentives.

briefingBlocks.heading: Your role and goal

briefingBlocks.text: Initial facts: the department has a backlog. A proposed reform introduces a dashboard ranking offices by the proportion of tickets closed within seven days. Supervisors will review that ranking each week. Staff can close a ticket after recording an action, even when the citizen has not confirmed that the issue is resolved. Citizen follow-up is feasible but currently separate from the dashboard.
briefingBlocks.heading: Proposed reform

briefingBlocks.caption: Before reform
notes: Resolution is reported by an independent random follow-up sample of 200 citizens. The dashboard measures speed and status, not verified resolution.

phases.title: Update response
facts: Results, revealed after initial submission: in the next month, 2,600 tickets are registered and 85% are closed within seven days. An independent random follow-up sample of 200 citizens finds 58% reporting resolution. Registration channels were expanded during that month, so more registered tickets do not necessarily mean more underlying problems. Some citizens report being asked to submit a new ticket if the issue persists after closure. The department has no comparison group or multi-month trend for this reform.
phases.task: Answer both questions. Evaluate which claims the dashboard and follow-up evidence support, then propose a warranted revision or retention of the reform.

prompts.label: Interpret the results
prompts.text: How do the results compare with your prediction? Explain what they support and what they do not establish. Consider a credible alternative explanation or a material limitation in the data.

prompts.label: Review your explanation and action
prompts.text: Which parts of your original causal explanation should you keep or revise, and why? What should you keep, revise or test in the proposed intervention? Connect both decisions to the results, state the remaining uncertainty, and identify the next useful evidence or test.

briefingBlocks.caption: Reported results
notes: Each resolution figure comes from an independent random follow-up sample of 200 citizens.
